intended_object: The classical group isomorphism Sp(1) ≅ SU(2): the unit Hamilton quaternions (norm 1), viewed as a group, are isomorphic to the special unitary group of 2×2 complex matrices, through the standard embedding ℍ → M₂(ℂ). This is taken from the docstring.
explanation:
`unitary ℍ[ℝ]` is the set of quaternions q with star q * q = 1 and q * star q = 1. These are exactly the unit quaternions, i.e. Sp(1). `Matrix.specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ` is SU(2).

The map sends q to `toComplexMatrix q`, which is the standard matrix [[a+bi, c+di], [−c+di, a−bi]]. The library already has this as a star-algebra homomorphism, so the restricted map preserves multiplication. The proof shows the map is injective (because `toComplexMatrix` is injective) and surjective onto SU(2), and `MulEquiv.ofBijective` turns this into a group isomorphism.

This is a specific, classical isomorphism, and its content needs this exact setting: real quaternions, complex 2×2 matrices and degree 2. So it is not too narrow. I searched Mathlib for `specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2)` and found no equivalent declaration.
